segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 12th, 2026.
We cover 20 key updates, including big news on humanoid robots, the Agility Robotics merger, and drone technology adoption.
Stay informed.
From Humanoids Daily, GXO signs a letter of intent for up to one thousand Apptronik Apollo humanoids.
This agreement establishes a framework for trials and the potential commercial deployment of the humanoid robots within GXO's logistics operations.

The collaboration involves testing the Apollo robots in GXO warehouses for logistics tasks including goods-to-person picking, case handling, packing, and sortation, all measured against predefined productivity and safety benchmarks.

If performance and safety targets are successfully met, the companies intend to deploy up to one thousand Apollo humanoids globally over a four-year period, commencing in North America in late two thousand twenty-seven.
Commercial deployment is projected under a Robotics-as-a-Service structure where GXO assumes the cost of the robots, building upon prior proof-of-concept work.
This development indicates a potential pathway for integrating advanced humanoid robotics into large-scale commercial logistics infrastructure.
From Robotics & Automation News, Agility Robotics completes a merger and secures four hundred sixty-five million dollars in capital ahead of a Nasdaq listing.
This report details the completion of a merger between Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI, which has resulted in a significant capital infusion necessary for future expansion.
The transaction was accomplished through a process that included a private investment in public offering financing led by Foxconn, which provided a portion of the capital.

This funding is designated to support the expansion of production and the commercial adoption of the company's humanoid robots, along with the preparation for the launch of the next-generation robot, Digit 5.
The combined entity is focused on translating commercial experience into growth while developing manufacturing and software solutions.
This development signals further movement in the commercialization of advanced robotics within the technology sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Bureau Veritas adopts Nolvis X1 drones for safer ship and offshore inspections.

This report details the utilization of Nolvis X1 drones for remote inspections of hazardous and confined spaces on ships and offshore installations, resulting in reduced safety risks associated with human entry into these environments.
The system is designed to operate in areas inaccessible to personnel, such as ballast tanks, without reliance on satellite navigation.
The drones collect visual and spatial data from these inaccessible locations, which is subsequently evaluated by certified marine surveyors.
This methodology supports a transition toward safer and more efficient digital asset management within the maritime industry.
This collaboration demonstrates a growing application of advanced robotics in high-risk industrial environments.
Future developments are expected to further integrate autonomous sensing into critical infrastructure monitoring.
From Robotics & Automation News, Cainiao introduces upgraded climbing robot with four-side retrieval and denser storage.
This report details enhancements made to climbing robots, resulting in a fifteen percent lift efficiency increase and a twenty percent storage density increase.
The updated systems incorporate four-side item retrieval and double-deep storage capacities.
This advancement was achieved through optimized movement incorporating smoother S-shaped turns, which enhanced operational efficiency during logistics tasks.
Furthermore, the technology includes a new warehouse planning simulation tool enabling rapid layout and investment assessment for diverse logistics scenarios.
International orders have already been secured for this technology.
This development signals further progress in autonomous material handling and warehouse optimization within the technology sector.
From Humanoids Daily, "Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial".
This report details a 24-hour trial where six AGIBOT G2 robots successfully completed 1,730 tasks within a Shanghai convenience store setting.
The robots performed a range of duties including customer assistance, product restocking, coffee preparation, and cleaning.
The operation was coordinated by the AGIBOT Genie Master framework, which utilized learning from both successful and unsuccessful attempts to refine performance.
Four of the six robots successfully passed the final assessment based on time, task completion, and the ability to handle unexpected situations.
This trial demonstrated the efficacy of embodied artificial intelligence in dynamic, real-world customer-facing environments.
Future developments in embodied AI are expected to focus on expanding practical deployment scenarios for such robotic systems.
From Humanoids Daily, Figure's Night-Shift "Robot Babysitter"
Is One of About 30 Jobs Keeping Its Humanoids Running.
This report details the hiring initiative by Figure to manage its humanoid robots across multiple global locations.

The company is currently seeking approximately thirty personnel for roles such as night-shift coordinators, robot operators, and data operation staff situated across the United States, Brazil, and Mexico.

These positions are categorized under Internal Fleet Operations, Commercial Operations, and Data Operations, encompassing responsibilities like supervising robot maintenance, operating the units, and piloting them to facilitate the teaching of new behaviors.
This staffing effort is designed to support Figure's objective of achieving continuous, twenty-four-seven robot operation and comprehensive data collection.
The expansion of this operational framework signals increasing integration of advanced robotics into continuous industrial processes.
From The Robot Report, Serve Robotics opens robot delivery network for others to build on.
This report details the launch of the AV Delivery Developer Portal, which provides access to the company's sidewalk delivery robots through an Application Programming Interface.
This portal establishes a sandbox environment enabling developers, businesses, and AI assistants to programmatically summon the robots for tasks.
The system allows users to build applications that request pickups and dropoffs, with Serve Robotics managing the complex routing and supervision of the delivery process.
This service is designed to allow users to develop applications that make daily errands more accessible through autonomous last-mile delivery solutions.
This development opens avenues for widespread application of autonomous robotics in commercial logistics.
From The Robot Report, Memories.ai builds standardized egocentric video pipeline.
This report details the development of a standardized pipeline to transform everyday egocentric video into training data for robotics.

The company labels footage using models such as Memories-H0 for hand pose and EgoAction for actions, providing a data infrastructure with egocentric video, custom annotation services, and dataset tools specifically for robot learning models.
Memories.ai processes and annotates data sourced from partners, emphasizing the processing of footage collected by those partners rather than wide-ranging collection.
The platform functions as a data-infrastructure partner for robotics and physical AI by tailoring data and potentially expanding into related models.
This advancement establishes a standardized methodology for creating high-quality, labeled training data essential for training sophisticated robotic systems.
Further developments in this data infrastructure are anticipated across the physical AI sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Niqo Robotics unveils a 50-foot AI weeder for large specialty crop farms, demonstrating advanced automation in agricultural management.
Niqo Robotics has introduced the RoboWeeder F50, a system designed for large specialty crop farms across North America.
This wide-format machine is engineered to perform three functions concurrently: precision weeding, thinning, and beneficial spraying.
The operation relies on Niqo's artificial intelligence, which rapidly trains algorithms to achieve high accuracy when identifying new crop types.
The F50 incorporates fourteen AI cameras and a three hundred fifty nozzle array to facilitate highly accurate pinpoint spraying across its entire width.
The robot is tractor-pulled and operates at a speed of up to four point seven miles per hour, supported by a local service team.
This development indicates a progression toward autonomous, multi-functional robotic systems in precision agriculture.

From Robotics & Automation News, FMC3 Robotics introduces the Doceo system to help industrial robots learn from factory workers, a system designed to enable industrial robots to learn manufacturing tasks by observing real-world human factory worker activities.

The system collects detailed physical-world data utilizing components such as Doceo RealCap, Hub, Cloud, and Driver to overcome the challenge of acquiring sufficient data for complex robot training outside of dedicated simulations.
This system establishes an industrial learning loop connecting task demonstrations with AI model development and robot operation.
FMC3 is also developing standardized data infrastructure through collaborations to ensure industrial training data is consistent and reusable.
This development signals a step toward more practical and data-efficient methods for training autonomous systems in industrial environments.
From Robotics & Automation News, Lincoln Electric introduces XpertLINC to bring physical AI to robotic welding.

This report details the introduction of a proprietary physical AI platform that dynamically adjusts robot paths and welding parameters to adapt to real-world conditions, resulting in improved productivity and quality.
The XpertLINC technology integrates vision, motion, and welding expertise to eliminate the need for extensive programming related to part fit-up and joint geometry.
The system achieves this by scanning parts to assess geometry and utilizing welding experience to automatically set parameters.
This innovation was initially launched on Cooper welding cobots, aiming to optimize manufacturing performance by automating welding intelligence.
The development signals a progression toward more autonomous and adaptable robotic manufacturing processes.
From Robotics & Automation News, ANYbotics begins deliveries of explosion-proof quadruped robot to industrial customers.

This report details the commencement of deliveries for the ANYmal X, a quadruped robot specifically engineered for inspection in explosive environments, demonstrating its application in oil, gas, and chemical facilities.
The ANYmal X incorporates explosion-protection measures such as sealed, nitrogen-filled chambers and flameproof casings for its battery and actuators.
The system autonomously conducts equipment inspections utilizing visual, thermal, acoustic, and gas sensors to identify faults without requiring facility modifications.
Furthermore, the technology integrates with existing maintenance systems to deliver end-to-end inspection solutions for hazardous settings.
This advancement signals the growing viability of autonomous robotics in high-risk industrial applications.
From Robotics & Automation News, Zipline makes drone deliveries quieter with real-time acoustic flight optimization.
This report details the implementation of sound-optimized dynamic flying utilizing onboard sound modeling to achieve significant reductions in noise pollution during drone deliveries.
The system employs real-time wind and altitude data to dynamically adjust transitions to on-wing flight, mimicking natural flight behaviors through sophisticated acoustic modeling.
This methodology resulted in a sixty-eight percent reduction in overall sound exposure per flight and twenty-four percent quieter flights at peak volume when compared to the twenty twenty five fleet.

Furthermore, this optimization reduces flight times by an average of fifty-three seconds and decreases energy consumption by twenty-one percent per flight, allowing for quieter operations and enabling future higher-altitude deployments.
This development signals advancements in integrating acoustic awareness with autonomous flight systems across the technology sector.

From Robotics & Automation News, Horkos integrates Meltio metal 3D printing technology into a new hybrid machining system, demonstrating the combination of additive manufacturing and subtractive methods in a single machine.
The new system, designated the NX70 Duo version AM, is a twin-head non-bed machining center that combines metal additive manufacturing with high-precision cutting.
This system successfully integrates additive and subtractive manufacturing capabilities by allowing for the alternating deposition of material and subsequent machining operations.
Meltio technology facilitates the precise deposition of metal through the use of laser energy and welding wire, enabling the production of complex parts, repairs, and prototypes.

This hybrid machine addresses manufacturing challenges related to labor shortages and space constraints by providing a highly automated solution that builds upon existing adoption of Meltio technology in CNC environments.
This integration supports various industries by offering advanced manufacturing solutions.
The development signals a trend toward highly integrated, multi-process manufacturing systems.
From Robotics & Automation News, CMS brings six-axis Krearob robotic 3D printing system to Formnext 2026.

This report details the debut of an advanced large format additive manufacturing system designed to produce large-scale thermoplastic tooling and components with significant material and weight savings.
The Krearob system integrates extrusion, slicing software, and human-machine interface for comprehensive control over the printing process.
This technology is capable of achieving up to eighty percent material and weight reductions.

The system is engineered for demanding manufacturing sectors including aerospace, automotive, and industrial applications, and CMS will also present the Kreator A3 system utilizing screw extrusion for large-format printing.
This development signals advancements in large-scale, complex geometry production methods for advanced engineering fields.
From Robotics & Automation News, Melotte reduces weekly 3D printing quality data handling from three hours to 20 minutes with amsight.
This report details the implementation of the amsight system designed to streamline the management of additive manufacturing quality data, achieving a significant reduction in data processing time.
Melotte implemented amsight to manage the collection and import of additive manufacturing quality information, a process that previously required approximately three hours per week.
The new system consolidates build, CT, sensor, and maintenance data into a traceable quality backbone.
This integration allows for significantly faster root-cause analysis, cutting investigation times from several hours down to under thirty minutes.
This technological advancement establishes a more efficient method for handling complex industrial data.
The integration of such systems indicates a trend toward more automated and interconnected data management across advanced manufacturing sectors.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Atlas on Wheels!".
This segment details an experimental configuration of the Atlas robot designed to study electric actuator performance through unusual locomotion.
The prototype utilizes scooter wheels attached to existing ankle motors to investigate demanding motor behavior while retaining the humanoid upper body.
The platform possesses capabilities for obstacle avoidance, jumping and landing, and sorting goods, although its overall skill score is noted as low.
Standing one hundred ninety centimeters tall and weighing ninety kilograms, the research focuses on the relationship between mobile navigation, actuator performance, and handling.
This configuration represents an experimental setup informing the final design of the Atlas robot.
This research provides data regarding the interaction between mobile navigation systems and complex actuator performance in humanoid robotics.
Future developments will likely build upon these findings to advance robotic locomotion capabilities.
From Robotics & Automation News, ESTUN Robotics integrates RoboDK simulation software to accelerate European expansion.

This story details a strategic partnership between ESTUN Robotics and RoboDK to combine their technologies for developing and simulating industrial robotic applications, resulting in an integrated solution.
The collaboration involved months of joint technical work to merge ESTUN's robot manufacturing capabilities with RoboDK's simulation and offline programming software.
This integration has been developed and refined, creating a satisfactory solution aimed at simplifying robotics adoption across Europe through enhanced simulation tools.
The alliance seeks to accelerate the delivery of complete, supported robotic solutions for European industry.
This development signals a step toward democratizing complex robotics through advanced simulation technology in the European industrial sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, Austrian Space Forum tests robotic rover for 2027 Mars analog mission at Gebrüder Weiss facility.
This report details testing of a robotic rover designed to assist crew with tool transport and navigation on Mars, which was conducted at the Gebrüder Weiss facility.
The testing involved systems developed by the University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria for the AMADEE-27 Mars analog mission.
Employees of Gebrüder Weiss observed the research activities firsthand during this process.

Gebrüder Weiss will manage the logistics for transporting sensitive research equipment to and from the mission site in Portugal in April 2027, where six analog astronauts will conduct experiments involving research from multiple international institutions.
This testing established operational procedures for robotic assistance in deep space simulation.
The successful testing advances practical applications for autonomous systems in future interplanetary exploration endeavors.
From Robotics & Automation News, Serve Robotics expands beyond US with DoorDash robot delivery launch in Australia.
This report details the launch of Australia's first footpath robot delivery service in the Gold Coast Health and Knowledge Precinct, demonstrating a pilot program for local delivery.
The initiative involved deploying robots that travel at a walking pace and operate under remote supervision for customers opting for deliveries from participating restaurants.

This project is designed to explore the integration of these robots as a complement to existing delivery methods for short, local trips, supporting DoorDash's multi-modal delivery strategy and engaging partnerships with Griffith University for research.
This development signals ongoing exploration of autonomous delivery systems within regional urban environments.
And that’s all the circuits for today!
Thinking about those Apollo humanoids signing their lease – the future is certainly getting more humanoid.
Thanks for tuning into your daily dose of robotic revelations.
Until tomorrow, keep building!
